title: The Genie part 2
reviewNotes: Four branches, 13 exact positions from three separate seven-piece diagrams after ...Qxb1. Qf5+ ...Qxf5 stalemates Kd4 with Bd2, or Ke3 with Bc3. The third stable board is Kd2 with Bd4, correcting captioned Ke2: Qh8+ ...Kg6 Qh7+ ...Kxh7 stalemates. Reusing Qf5 in that third cage loses because Kc1 remains legal. Earlier nine/eight-piece sequence is context, not certified.
transcript: The genie gives you this position and he tells you that he's going to grant you three wishes if you manage to survive with white. You look at the board and you quickly realize that you only have a knight and a bishop left against an entire queen and two bishops. But this puzzle must have some kind of solution and you notice that you have a pawn that is only one square away from getting a new piece. You start by considering the promotion to a queen, but unfortunately this wouldn't work because the genie can start giving you some checks and at the right time pick up this knight and be completely You notice that you can also promote to a knight, but this doesn't work either. The king is simply going to go to the corner and there is no follow up. But then you find a brilliant idea that allows you to promote to the queen with a check. Knight to F8 check. Now of course the only move available to the king is to go to H8 and now you follow up with the brilliant knight to G6 check. Going back up now wouldn't make any sense because now you could promote to a knight and actually checkmate black. But the genie is not that naive and so he just picks up this knight and now you are able to promote to a queen with a check. The only move for black is king H7 and now it seems like black is simply out of the woods. But you follow up calmly with bishop to B1. A move that doesn't seem to make sense. You're blundering yet another piece. Of course the genie has to take otherwise the queen is pinned to the king and you're going to take it on the next move. But he's very glad to do that and the genie is smiling as he takes the bishop. But his smirk fades away as you play the last of your brilliant moves. Queen to F5 check. Forking the king and queen. And now of course if the genie were to take this queen this would be a beautiful stalemate and a draw, which is why the genie stops you and he tells you, "No, no, no. I want to change my move." And he goes back to the moment when you played bishop to B1 and he now decides to give you a check with this bishop. If you don't have the right setup for the stalemate, he's just going to be able to pick up this bishop and win the game. You have no choice but to move your king. And so, you move it to E3. The genie picks up the bishop. And now you hit him with queen to F5 check again. Because what the genie failed to realize is that this is going to be another stalemate and another draw. So, as you're about to play queen F5, the genie stops you and he tells you, "No, I want to change my move one last time." And he goes back to this moment when you moved your king and he gives you another check with the bishop. You play king to E2. And now the queen is indeed free to take here because queen F5 would fail. This would not be a stalemate. But that is not a problem because the white king is already stalemated. And so, all we have to do is to give up the queen, queen to H8. The king doesn't want to take the queen, king G6. But now we force him to with queen to H7. If the king moves, we're going to win the queen. So, the genie takes. And this is yet again another stalemate. Follow for more.
